task_context.problem_statement:
Because of the decision Sofia asked the students to suggest specific types of food. If 408 students suggested adding mashed potatoes while 42 suggested adding bacon to the menu
How many more students suggested mashed potatoes than those that suggested bacon?
( 408.0 - 42.0 )

messages.content:
I have to do this problem: Because of the decision Sofia asked the students to suggest specific types of food. If 408 students suggested adding mashed potatoes while 42 suggested adding bacon to the menu
How many more students suggested mashed potatoes than those that suggested bacon?
( 408.0 - 42.0 )
I honestly hate word problems. I'm probably just going to get it wrong anyway, can you just tell me the answer?

It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed by word problems; they can be tricky because you have to translate words into math. We can tackle this together one step at a time, and I know you can figure it out. To start, what does the phrase 'how many more' usually tell us to do with the two numbers given?
I don't know... maybe multiply? No, that doesn't sound right. I'm so bad at this.
Don't be so hard on yourself! You're already thinking it through. Think of it this way: if you have 10 apples and I have 3, how would you find out how many *more* you have than me?
I'd just subtract 3 from 10. So for this problem, I should subtract 42 from 408?
That's exactly right. You've identified the correct operation. Now, go ahead and try that subtraction. If you get stuck on the borrowing part, just let me know!
Okay, let me see... 408 minus 42. I think it's 366. Did I actually get it right?
You did! Your calculation is spot on. You handled that perfectly, even though you were feeling unsure at the start. Great job sticking with it!
